applies_why: The judge text resolves the D5-versus-C5 link by declaring Isaiah 7:14 underdetermined because its sign-sense is open, which is a verse-level determination of a contested link.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse' — I weighed whether treating Isaiah 7:14's sign-sense as open is a forbidden verse-by-verse resolution or merely a permissible finding that the link lacks footing.
why: The judge makes the open sense of Isaiah 7:14 decisive for D5 versus C5, so it decides the link at the verse level rather than weighing the parties' chains by footing as K-C requires.
